description: In an augmented-reality rubber hand illusion, a virtual hand pulsing in time with the participant's heartbeat raised both questionnaire ownership and proprioceptive drift compared with out-of-time pulsing. The effect was absent when finger movements were remapped onto the virtual hand.
limitations: Effects held in the cardiac still condition only, and ownership questionnaires and proprioceptive drift do not always agree.

sources.quote: both subjective and objective measures of virtual-hand ownership are enhanced by cardio-visual feedback in-time with the actual heartbeat, as compared to asynchronous feedback
PDDs were significantly larger for synchronous versus asynchronous cardio-visual feedback in the 'cardiac still' (without finger movements), but not the 'cardiac move' condition
